name: Amigo
devices_driven: one standard steerable EP catheter handle (Boston Scientific Blazer or Biosense Webster EZ Steer orientation, docking station specific to the catheter type); no proprietary catheters, introducers or sheaths (catheterrobotics2020_amigo_BROCHURE pp. 3, 7)
translation_detail: other: mechanical cradle moving catheter handle
device_range: linear translation < 12 +- 2 mm/s; linear resolution < 1.6 mm; rotation resolution < 1.1 deg; rotation max < 0.42 rev/s; articulation resolution 1.0% full scale; articulation max 0.48 rev/s (brochure p. 3)
footprint_mm: 1016 x 1372 x 1118 mm (H x W x D; converted by X2 from 40 x 54 x 44 in as listed, whole robot) (brochure p. 3)
mass_kg: approx. 70 lb = 31.8 kg (converted by X2) (brochure p. 3)
haptics_leader: no: handheld remote controller like a catheter handle (rotation knob, deflection knob, insert and withdraw buttons), up to 100 ft away (brochure p. 5)
imaging_compat: uses existing EP-lab monitors and workstations, no room rebuild (brochure p. 3)
sterility: disposable kit: drapes over the sides and top, nosecone to the introducer, catheter track, docking station and spreader form the sterile interface (brochure p. 7)
validation_detail: IDE trial NCT01139814: 206 patients enrolled at 13 centres, 8 pre-specified locations each, 1,448 locations mapped (brochure p. 1); 181-pt analysis 1,396/1,448 (96%) (PMC7252924 via search, not opened)
key_numbers: efficacy 96% (97% adjusted for missing source data; 99% with fluoroscopic confirmation only); responder success (6 of 8 locations) 98%; mean manipulation time 45 s per location, falling significantly by the 3rd case; no major complications, no perforations (brochure p. 1); FDA K122488 (2012): manipulation of diagnostic catheters in RA/RV only, ablation not established (510k.innolitics via search summary)
